### Diagnosis
The test `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinterTest.testMySqlNullStringDefault()` is failing because it expects the MySQL null string representation (`"\\N"`) to be returned by `CSVFormat.MYSQL.getNullString()`. However, the `getNullString()` method in `CSVFormat` class simply returns the `nullString`, which is a field used for the string representation of null values. Therefore, the test fails as it is comparing `nullString` (which is probably null) to `"\\N"`.

The issue here is that the `CSVFormat.MYSQL.getNullString()` method should directly return `"\\N"` instead of relying on the `nullString` field.

### Suggestions for Fix
- `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.MYSQL.getNullString()` (Change the implementation to directly return `"\\N"`)

Please proceed with the suggested fix.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
